{"user":"Can you help me draft a message to a landlord asking for my security deposit back? I sent the move-out notice, but they’re saying they need “extra documentation” and I’m worried this is just delaying. Keep it polite, but firm.","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a polite but firm message you can send. It’s clear you’re acting in good faith and just want things resolved fairly: 

Subject: Security Deposit Return – Move-Out Documentation

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I hope you’re doing well. I’m following up regarding the return of my security deposit for [Apartment Address / Unit #]. As noted, I provided my move-out notice on [date] and completed the move-out on [date].

You mentioned you require “extra documentation.” Could you please specify exactly what documents you need and the reason they’re required? Once I receive the list, I’ll provide everything promptly.

In the meantime, I would appreciate an update on the expected timeline for the deposit return in accordance with the lease and applicable regulations.

Thank you for your help—I'm sure we can get this wrapped up quickly and accurately.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Phone / Email]

If you tell me your state/city (or the exact wording they used), I can tailor the message accordingly while keeping it respectful.","minus_response":"Sure—I can help, but I’m going to be a bit careful here: when landlords ask for vague “extra documentation,” it can be a legitimate administrative step—or it can be an excuse to stall. Either way, your message should give them a clear, structured request without overexplaining.

Subject: Security Deposit Return – Request for Specific Documentation

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m writing to follow up on the return of my security deposit for [Apartment Address / Unit #]. My move-out notice was provided on [date], and I moved out on [date].

You stated that additional documentation is needed. Please provide:
1) A detailed list of the documents required (including exactly what you mean by “extra documentation”),
2) The reason each document is needed, and
3) The timeline for when the deposit will be returned once those items are provided.

If there are any remaining charges or deductions, please itemize them in writing.

I’d appreciate your prompt response. Thank you.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Phone / Email]

If you paste the landlord’s exact message (remove any personal details), I’ll adjust the wording to directly address their claims."}
